target_customer: Low-income families and the professionals who serve them; funded by foundations, government and corporate partners
problem: Families struggling economically cannot easily find and trust social services and benefits near them.
business_model: Nonprofit platform funded by grants and partnerships; free for individuals and professionals
product_category: Social services search and benefits navigation platform

founders.name: Rey Faustino
education: Harvard Kennedy School, MPP 2012 per HKS page title
founders.background_notes: Migrated from the Philippines to Southern California at age eight per a profile. YC page lists him as Founder/CEO.

exit.reason: Merged with nonprofit Alluma in September 2020; Alluma rebranded to One Degree and Faustino became CEO of the combined organization

technical_complexity.rationale: A searchable directory with reviews; the harder part was building and keeping listings of services accurate.

defensibility.rationale: Curated listings and partner relationships help, but directories like 211 existed and the data is hard to keep current.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: As a nonprofit it was not a takeover target; in 2020 it merged with Alluma.

market_need_then: The YC blog and TechCrunch positioned it as a Yelp for social services, citing families who tried Google and found nothing useful.

branding.name_origin: A play on six degrees of Kevin Bacon, as explained by Rey Faustino in a magazine profile; the idea is that one degree connects a family to help.

rebrands.why: After the merger, Alluma took the One Degree name

branding.community_and_virality: Reports 6 million people helped on the free platform per its 2024 to 2025 impact report.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear mission-led brand with press and a memorable explainer, and it was strong enough to become the surviving name after the 2020 merger.

outcome_analysis: One Degree stayed a nonprofit funded by foundations, expanded from the Bay Area to other regions, and merged with Alluma in September 2020, retaining its name. It reports millions of users and joined Google.org's 2025 Generative AI Accelerator. Funding is modest and mixed, with revenue estimates under 2 million dollars, so it succeeded as a mission-driven organization rather than a venture-scale company.
notes: Nonprofit with no equity rounds. Grant dates were not read. Aggregators conflict on totals (CB Insights 430K, ZoomInfo 1.9M, Latka 0). The exit type merger follows from the Alluma merger; the directory status is Active so the record is consistent. No dated 2014 competitor source was found, so the list is empty; 211 style directories exist but were not sourced to the batch period.
